questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good university with a different university culture than what we have at UCPH. A city I was eager to explore and good recommendations from previous students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was available from the partner university. They did completely bombard me with unnecessary information so I had to sort though important and non important info.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a bit of assistance from their international office. Overall the assistance and proactivity from the study destination should have been way better though. I was lucky to get a nice big group of friends very quickly. If that didn't happen I would have been at a big risk of being lonely, as there was very few social events or introduction to other exchanges.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The most imporatant information was definetely available, but the rest was lacking.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. There is many resources available such as facebook groups subleasing. or googling finding the large apartment complexes who will often have a room available. It is however very expensive (Expect Copenhagen prices)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a large co-op off campus. This was a good way to meet new people and save some money on rent/food. It is dirty and noisy so definitely not for everyone, but the social side will probably make it worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: America has a lot of visa requirements. A lot of time/money and documentation is necessary.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They will send you a list of 20-30 steps to complete.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was pretty straight forward, but I recall that they had a contact person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes offered a lot of good learning opportunities, but also a lot of unnecessary readings.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They were a lot less method oriented. This means a lot of readings that can feel unnecessary at times and not a lot of practical usage of the law.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contract for foreign lawyers, International human rights law, Intellectual property (intro), wind and solar law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Intellectual property is a very good intro, where most of the taught rules will either be applicable or close to applicable in a European country. The teacher was also amazing but sadly retired.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. The University has some "bullshit" fees that I don't expect are encountered by students gong the other way. Apart from that expect high prices as Austin is very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food at campus was very expensive. It was hard to get a lunch for under 10 dollars in my area of campus. a cheap option was panda express at 8.5 dollars. This will quickly run up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had very nice grounds for both tennis, swimming, working out etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Very many student orgs offer a lot. The uni also has a lot of different. 
Just remember to search them out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking trips with UT rec is a good way to meet people. The same with the intramural sports etc. Take the opportunities given and you will have a good time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot of nice food/drink options. Take some trips out of town and experience the US. It has a lot to offer!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Make an effort to start off with. 
Note that most western exchange student tend to be left together as the americans generally tick to themselves.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping culture is very weird when you are not used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Seeing rodeos, shooting etc was very fun. All the nice little niche cafes etc was also very interesting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have an open mind, bring a lot of money and remember to get the big ticket and watch a lot of sports (also just for the social aspect).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling into a life without any of your friends in a time zone far away from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
